title: What Washington May Misread in Brazil’s Election
gist: Fernanda Magnotta argues Washington may overestimate how much Brazil's October 2026 election (Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro) will change Brazil's stance: China takes 30.7% of exports and a cross-party consensus, now codified in Law 15,506, demands domestic value-addition in critical minerals. US access will require capital and offtake packages like Serra Verde's, not political affinity.

themes.theme: Election contrast is narrower than it looks

insights.claim: Lula's platform centers strategic autonomy, BRICS and the Global South, while Flávio Bolsonaro promises to repair US ties and engage the OECD, but neither amounts to a binary choice between Washington and Beijing.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Avoid pricing a Bolsonaro win as a decisive pro-US realignment of Brazil.
insights.quote: Yet this does not translate neatly into a choice between Washington and Beijing.

insights.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro says he favors negotiating with everyone from China to the EU to the US while avoiding excessive dependence on any one partner.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Signals continuity of multi-alignment trade policy under a right-wing government.
insights.quote: “from China to the European Union, from the United States to Asian markets,”

insights.claim: Brazil's core interests, frameworks and institutions will not change much regardless of who wins, continuing to define posture on China trade and critical minerals.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Election-driven volatility in Brazil-China trade or mining policy expectations may be overdone.
insights.quote: Brazil’s core interests, frameworks, and institutions will not change much

themes.theme: China's structural grip on Brazil's trade

insights.claim: In the first eight months of the year, China absorbed 30.7% of Brazilian exports versus 9.6% for the United States.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Brazil's export economy is over three times more exposed to China than to the US.
insights.quote: China absorbed 30.7% of Brazilian exports, compared with 9.6% for the U.S.

insights.claim: Jair Bolsonaro campaigned in 2018 warning China was 'buying Brazil' but in office turned pragmatic and left Huawei eligible for 5G despite US pressure, largely because agribusiness protected its largest market.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Precedent that anti-China rhetoric yields to economic structure once in power.

insights.claim: Agribusiness, with China as the leading buyer of Brazilian soybeans and farm exports, is the lobby that constrains any Brazilian government's alignment against Beijing.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Brazil's agri sector is a structural anchor of China ties, limiting tail-risk of trade rupture.

insights.claim: A CEBRI/Vallya study for Brazil's Ministry of Mines and Energy estimates China holds about 70% of world rare-earth production and 94% of magnet manufacturing.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Quantifies the concentration risk driving Western demand for alternative rare-earth supply.
insights.quote: China accounts for about 70% of the world’s rare-earth production and 94% of magnet manufacturing

insights.claim: Brazil holds an estimated 23.1% of the world's rare earths, with reserves of 21 million metric tons.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Makes Brazil a core node in any non-China rare-earth supply chain.
insights.quote: Brazil holds an estimated 23.1% of the world’s rare earths, with reserves of 21 million metric tons.

insights.claim: Both Lula (state-coordinated reindustrialization) and Flávio Bolsonaro (market-oriented, faster licensing) reject raw-material exports and prioritize domestic processing and local employment.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Expect value-addition requirements on Brazilian minerals regardless of election outcome.

insights.claim: Brazil's new Law 15,506 makes domestic value addition, technology transfer and sovereignty key objectives of critical-minerals policy and allows screening of control changes, foreign influence, mining-rights transfers and supply agreements.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Foreign investors in Brazilian minerals face a new screening and value-add regime raising deal complexity.

insights.claim: Law 15,506 permits export-related value-addition requirements and creates a monitoring council including states, municipalities, companies and universities, and passed with cross-party support.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Cross-party backing makes the regime durable across administrations.
insights.quote: It specifically allows export-related value-addition requirements and creates a council to monitor these factors

insights.claim: Rare-earth projects require approvals from Congress, the National Mining Agency, environmental and local authorities and communities, and thorium content can add nuclear-safety regulators, so no president controls the supply chain unilaterally.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Project timelines in Brazilian rare earths will be long and multi-veto, regardless of political will.

insights.claim: The Serra Verde acquisition in Goiás came with a 15-year offtake for 100% of Phase I production, guaranteed floor prices and $565 million of DFC financing.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Template for Western critical-mineral deals: price floors, offtakes and state finance.
insights.quote: a 15-year agreement covering 100% of Phase I production, guaranteed floor prices, and a $565 million financing deal

insights.claim: Political affinity will not automatically translate into commercial access or strategic control; the US must offer capital, risk protection and treat Brazil as a value-chain partner, not a commodity supplier.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: US-Brazil mineral deals will carry higher costs and local-processing conditions.
insights.quote: political affinity will not automatically translate into commercial access or strategic control

insights.claim: A Bolsonaro administration might prioritize faster decisions and US-backed investment while a Lula government might demand stricter conditions, affecting project selection and bargaining style rather than direction.
insights.speaker: FERNANDA MAGNOTTA
insights.so_what: Election outcome matters at the margin for deal speed and terms.
